JUBILANT FOODWORKS Q2 BIZ: Q2 CONSOLIDATED REVENUE RISES 11.9% YOY; DOMINO’S INDIA LFL GROWTH AT 4.1%

• Consolidated revenue from operations at ₹2,608.7 Cr, up 11.9% YoY.
• Standalone revenue from operations at ₹1,885.8 Cr, up 11.6% YoY.
• Domino’s India Like-for-Like (LFL) growth stood at 4.1%.
• Domino’s Eurasia LFL growth declined 2.1%.
• JFL added net 108 stores during Q2, taking total group store count to 3,820.
• Domino’s India added 88 stores, taking total to 2,601 stores.
• Domino’s Eurasia added 3 stores, taking total to 798 stores.

BHARAT FORGE : LITIGATION APPEAL DISMISSED

• Company's appeal regarding litigation involving Mr. Tarsem Jain dismissed by Delhi High Court vide order dated October 1, 2026.
• The appeal challenged the order dated May 26, 2025, by the learned Single Judge of the Delhi High Court, which had set aside the arbitral award.
• The detailed disclosures made on May 27, 2025, stand amended to the extent mentioned above.
Impact: Positive (Favorable court decision reduces ongoing litigation risk)

INDOTHAI SECURITIES RAISED RS 2.35 CR FUNDS FROM NCDS ON PRIVATE PLACEMENT

• Allotted 235 Secured, Redeemable, Unlisted, Unrated, Non-Convertible Debentures (NCDs) of face value ₹1,00,000 each.
• Total allotment value of ~₹2.35 Cr, aggregating to ₹2.35 Cr under Tranche-I.
• The NCDs are unlisted securities and have a tenure of 370 or 1101 days from the allotment date.
• Coupon/Interest Rate is 9.50% or 9.90% per annum, with quarterly and annual payment options.
• In case of default, additional interest of 2% p.a. over the interest rate will be charged.
Impact: Funding raised through NCDs.

MATRIMONY.COM LTD : Q2 BIZ 

• Consolidated billings for the quarter ended Sep 30, 2026, stood at ₹13,109 Lakhs, a 10.7% YoY growth from ₹11,844 Lakhs in the prior year.
• For the half year ended Sep 30, 2026, consolidated billings were ₹26,711 Lakhs, up 9.2% YoY from ₹24,461 Lakhs in the prior year.

FINO PAYMENTS BANK LTD : BUSINESS HIGHLIGHTS – SEPTEMBER 2026

• Deposit accounts opened decreased 17% YoY to 2,44,763 in September'26.
• Renewal income increased 20% YoY to ₹28.0 Cr in September'26.
• Average total deposits grew 13% YoY to ₹2,794 Cr in September'26.
• Digitally active customers increased 13% YoY to 64.9 Lakh in September'26.
• FinoPay active customers rose 12% YoY to 8.1 Lakh in September'26.
• Transaction business throughput decreased 10% YoY to ₹3,469 Cr in September'26.
• CMS throughput increased 10% YoY to ₹6,918 Cr in September'26.

PNB HOUSING FINANCE : CREDIT RATING UPGRADED TO AAA FROM CRISIL

• PNB Housing Finance receives credit rating upgrade to 'AAA' from CRISIL; marking a full suite of rating upgrades across all four agencies.
• CRISIL Ratings has upgraded its long-term rating to 'CRISIL AAA/Stable' from ‘CRISIL AA+/Stable’.
• The upgrades reflect the strengthening of the Company's financial and operating fundamentals, including improving asset quality, strong capitalisation, enhanced profitability, and a granular retail-focused mortgage portfolio.
Impact: Positive

BANK OF INDIA : REVISED LENDING RATE TO 8.35%

• Bank's Repo Based Lending Rate (RBLR) revised to 5.50% with immediate effect from October 7, 2026.
• The revision is due to an upward revision in the Repo Rate announced by RBI.
• The new RBLR is effective from 07-10-2026, with Repo Rate at 5.50% and Mark up at 2.85%.
• Effective RBLR stands at 8.35%, an increase of 25 bps from the previous rate.

Impact: Neutral (Regulatory update on lending rate)

SANOFI INDIA : PROMOTER GROUP ENTITY ACQUIRES SHARES FROM HOECHST GMBH

• Sanofi Healthcare India Private Limited, an entity part of the promoter group, acquired 3,500,000 equity shares of Sanofi India Limited from Hoechst GmbH on September 24, 2026.
• This acquisition, an inter-se transfer among promoter group members, falls under Regulation 10(1)(a)(iii) of SAST Regulations.
• The aggregate holding of the promoter and promoter group remains unchanged.
• Intimations under Regulation 10(5) and 10(6) were filed on September 17 and September 28, 2026, respectively.
• Fees of ₹1,77,000 have been remitted for the report.
Impact: Neutral (Regulatory filing for a promoter group share transfer under exemption)

LEO DRYFRUITS & SPICES TRADING LIMITED : PRINCIPAL SPONSORSHIP OF RAJASTHAN SPIKERS FOR VOLLEYBALL CHAMPIONS LEAGUE SEASON 1

• The company has been confirmed as the Principal Sponsor of Rajasthan Spikers for Season 1 of the Volleyball Champions League (VCL).
• The arrangement has been confirmed by Bakliwal Volleysports Pvt. Ltd., the management of Rajasthan Spikers.
• The Volleyball Champions League Season 1 is being held at Noida from October 06, 2026 to October 23, 2026.
• Deliverables include front chest jersey placement, Sony Sports & SonyLIV FCT inventory (250 seconds), Aston Ad, on-ground branding, social media posts, hospitality, and player engagement opportunities.
• The arrangement also includes category exclusivity and additional brand integrations.
Impact: Positive (Enhances brand visibility and promotional opportunities through association with the VCL and Rajasthan Spikers.)

H-ACID | MANUFACTURING COMPLEXITY + INDIA OPPORTUNITY

Value Chain
- Naphthalene → H-Acid.
- H-Acid → Dye intermediates.
- Dye intermediates → Reactive/Acid/Direct dyes.
- Dyes → Textiles, leather, paper and applications.

Why H-Acid Is Difficult
- Conventional route involves multiple chemical stages.
- Naphthalene → Sulphuric acid/Oleum.
- Nitric acid → Reduction.
- Caustic soda → Alkali fusion.
- High-temperature and high-pressure processing required.
- Final stages involve acidification and purification.

Environmental Complexity
- Process generates significant waste.
- Requires serious ETP/ZLD infrastructure.
- Installed capacity may not equal effective capacity.
- Compliant and efficient capacity matters more.

India China+1 Opportunity
- Environmental restrictions can remove inefficient capacity.
- Customers seek reliable non-China suppliers.
- India has established dye-intermediate chemistry.
- Gujarat and Maharashtra have mature ecosystems.
- Indian textiles provide a large downstream market.

Competitive Advantage
- Reliability can matter more than lowest cost.
- Compliant producers may gain pricing power.
- Supply constraints can support sharper pricing.
- Effective capacity is the key industry metric.

Listed H-Acid Exposure
- Shree Hari Chemicals: closest pure-play exposure.
- Bhageria Industries: H-Acid + Vinyl Sulphone.
- AksharChem India: H-Acid + Vinyl Sulphone.
- AksharChem also has pigments and silica.
- Bodal Chemicals: broad dye-intermediate ecosystem.
- Kiri Industries: integrated H-Acid + Vinyl Sulphone.
- Kiri also has dyes and basic chemicals.

Business Model Spectrum
- Pure-play → Higher H-Acid sensitivity.
- Integrated → Diversified chemical exposure.
- Pure-play offers higher H-Acid beta.
- Integrated players offer broader ecosystems.

KEY TAKEAWAY
H-Acid manufacturing is complex, waste-intensive and environmentally demanding. The opportunity may therefore depend more on effective compliant capacity than installed capacity, with reliable Indian producers potentially benefiting from China+1 demand.

What regulators see that investors often ignore 👇

Every time a regulator acts, investors first ask: "How much EPS gets hit?" Regulators ask something else: "Is the market structure fair for the end consumer?" That's a very different lens. 
Thoughts on recent #PBFintech & older #IEX n more

Case in point: Recent change on insurance commissions. The proposed changes effectively aim to reduce distribution costs & curb excessive upfront payouts on some products. Investors see lower margins. Regulators see lower customer acquisition costs & better value for policyholders.

Truth is, hardly anyone argues that insurance has zero mis-selling. Higher upfront commissions have often created incentives to sell what pays the most, not what suits the customer best. If that problem exists, intervention shouldn't be surprising.

The irony is that many investors celebrate efficiency in every industry except their own portfolio holdings. When a regulator targets excess distribution costs, the reaction is often outrage instead of introspection.

Look at insurance expense ratios. Even as the industry scaled up, commission/expense pools as a % of premium remained elevated in several segments. The regulator's job is to ask: why isn't scale translating into lower customer costs?

Learning from MFs TER. Every TER cut was seen as fatal attack. Prediction was: growth will die, distributors will vanish, profit collapse. Instead industry adapted. Players became efficient, direct plans gained share, technology reduced costs, investor participation & AUM surged

Market coupling in power exch. Investors focus: which exchange lose market share. Regulators focus: consumers get better price discovery. Market coupling means bids/orders from all exch get pooled to discover a single price. One price improves efficiency & reduces fragmentation

Could one exchange lose moat? Maybe. But from system perspective, better price discovery, deeper liquidity & lower market distortion are hard to ignore.
Regulators rarely optimize for shareholder returns. They optimize for consumers, market efficiency & long-term public interest

Think about hospitals. If tomorrow there is stricter price regulation, hospital stocks may get hit. As investors we'd feel the pain. But can anyone honestly deny healthcare costs are becoming unaffordable for a large section of Indians?
One may argue India's healthcare is still cheaper than many countries. True. But the person comparing prices globally is not the same person struggling to pay a hospital bill locally.

Markets often assume regulators must protect industry profitability. Regulators believe industries shouldn't fleece poor customers. When public benefit & industry profits collide, the regulator's choice is usually obvious.

That's why stock market reaction is often the last variable in the regulator's decision. If a policy improves consumer outcomes, transparency, affordability or efficiency, temporary shareholder pain rarely changes the outcome.

Tata Group Boardroom Tug of War
Some history repeat; Some history rhyme
30 yrs ago it was Ratan Tata vs Russi Mody. Today, many see shades of that battle in the Chandra vs Noel Tata face-off
Back in the 1990s, Ratan Tata was consolidating authority within a sprawling Tata empire run by powerful Operating entity heads. Russi Mody was among the most influential Tata executives of his era. Larger-than-life personality, huge public profile & massive influence within the group.
Ratan Tata believed Tata Group needed one strategic centre of gravity. Not multiple power centres running individual fiefdoms. Eventually, Russi Mody exited & Ratan Tata tightened control over the conglomerate.
Fast forward three decades.
The debate is again centred around leadership, control & the future direction of Tata Sons. This time its Noel Tata, who chairs Tata Trusts, & N Chandrasekaran, who leads Tata Sons
Key contentions are Chandra’s reappointment as chairman & Tata Sons listing. Noel Tata has opposed both
The striking part? Tata Sons board backed Chandra by a 4:1 vote, while Noel Tata stood opposed
Russi Mody took the battle public. Media interviews, public sparring & headline-grabbing exchanges became part of the story.
Chandra, however, has largely stayed silent in public
Whether history repeats or merely echoes, one thing is clear
Generational change of Tata leadership eventually confronts the same question.

Is India investing enough for future capacity

India is usually described as a consumption economy. Consumption contributes >60% of GDP. But the story becomes incomplete when we ignore what's happening on the investment side and other aspects of our economy

India's Gross Capital Formation is ~32.6% of GDP. Lower than China's ~40%, but China's per capita GDP is several times of India's. Comparing ratios without considering income levels misses the context.

A developing country cannot allocate every ₹ toward factories & infra. A large share of resources must also support the bottom of the pyramid through housing, healthcare, education & welfare.

A harmonious society requires a minimum standard of living for those at the bottom. India is building capacity while simultaneously funding social stability. That's a tougher balancing act than many realize.

Cement tells the same story. India produces ~400 MT annually out of ~4,000 MT globally. Again, roughly 10% global share despite only ~3.5% share of world GDP. Countries don't consume steel & cement at this scale unless they are building physical assets. These are the raw materials of future GDP.

Power generation presents a slightly different picture. India's share of global electricity output is lower than steel & cement, but still materially ahead of its global GDP share. India with 1800bn units vs 32,000bn units, 6% global share

The scale of projects are also changing. DFCs, industrial corridors, semiconductor fabs, renewable energy parks, metros, airports, transmission corridors & logistics networks are larger than anything India attempted before.

If this trend continues, India's share of global steel, cement & power usage is likely to keep rising. Higher material intensity today is often a precursor to higher economic output tomorrow.

De-Dollarization lets peek into central bank reserves

They're moving into something with no issuer at all: Gold. Central banks themselves are now one of the biggest sources of gold demand globally, roughly buy ~30% of annual global mine production

Gold isn't rising only because investors are bullish. Significant chunk of global prodn is locked away by sovereign balance sheets. In 2026, central banks gold buying at slower pace vs 2025 due to 60% price rise.

Among the Major buyers were Poland, China, Brazil, India etc. 
Then there are few sellers too. Turkey has been among the largest sellers this year, reportedly selling ~83t YTD to support liquidity & FX/US$ needs.

Real story is different from "the end of the USD."
Reserve diversification is real.
Dollar replacement is not. Not in near future

Birla trying to replicate Paint like disruption in Wire & Cables
India's W&C industry is a INR 1.1trn & growing at ~13% CAGR. Despite its size (0.3% of India GDP), industry remains fragmented with top 6 players control ~50% share

Market is roughly split into 3 equal buckets: Wires, LT Cables & MV/HT/EHV/Specialized Cables. Cables compared to wire is more organized, house wires have larger unorganized participation. Overall unorganized is > 30%

what attracted Birla. W&C sits at the intersection of electrification, urbanization & digitization. Housing, infra, renewables, data centres & manufacturing all need more wires.

Ultratech has launched Ultravolt with planned capex of ₹18 bn. Initial plant capacity has already started production ahead of schedule at Bharuch. The market compares this with the paint disruption. Lets look at numbers

Grasim's paint capex was ~65-70% of Asian Paint. Ultravolt's ₹18 bn capex is 30% of Polycab gross block. Plus, Polycab's gross block is expected to reach ~₹94 bn in FY28 while KEI could reach ~₹43 bn. Ultravolt's announced gross block is only ₹18 bn

The biggest advantage for Ultratech is raw material availability. Copper & Aluminium dominate industry economics and the Birla ecosystem already has deep expertise & inhouse production

Demand-intelligence advantage. Cement is purchased 6 months before wires in building construction. Ultratech can potentially spot demand trends 4-6 months ahead of competitors

Builder relationships, contractor network & Ultratech Building Solutions outlets create a ready-made ecosystem for cross-selling wires. That's a powerful advantage most new entrant

Ultravolt has prepared well. Better channel incentives, faster delivery commitments, aggressive marketing & strong retailer engagement are already creating buzz. But replicating the paint playbook won't be straightforward. 

Paints & cement share significant overlap in distribution. Wires are largely sold through electrical dealers, distributors, retailers & electrician networks. Building an electrical distribution franchise takes years

Another key difference is profitability. Leading W&C players operate at ~12-14% EBITDA margins, far lower than the 18-20%+ margins paint Co. enjoyed before disruption. With lower margins, room for aggressive pricing is limited

Further: Utility, industrial, railway, transmission & infra projects require extensive testing, approvals, certifications & execution history before meaningful scale can be achieved.
Conclusion: Birla has genuine advantage in raw material sourcing, builder relationships & demand visibility. But unlike paints, incumbents start with lower margins, stronger technical moats & entrenched distribution

Coforge Chairman resignation : Lets dig deeper

OP Bhatt's resignation came after disagreements around the Board evaluation process. In his resignation note, he says continuing on Board amid differences regarding his "good faith actions" would not be conducive to Board effective functioning 

OP Bhatt is not a conventional IT industry chairman. He is among India's most respected bankers, having led SBI between 2006-11 & later served on boards across large corporates including Tata Group companies

The market doesn’t take such update kindly, but Bhatt's continuation was already under question even before the resignation. Shareholders (inc largest shareholder Advent) voted against his reappointment as Independent Director from May'27
 
Let’s go a bit in history: The company was earlier known as NIIT Tech before its ownership transition & eventual rebranding to Coforge. Barings acquired control of NIIT in 2020, leading to ownership change then.

Later, Barings steadily monetised its stake through multiple block deals as the company scaled in size, profitability & market value. After Barings' complete exit by FY24, Co. become fully public market institutional owned.

OP Bhatt joined the board in 2024 & became Chairman during a phase when Coforge was pursuing aggressive scale-up ambitions. Coforge accelerated inorganic growth. The acquisition of Cigniti significantly expanded its engineering & digital capabilities under him.

The much bigger acquisition Encora was also under OP Bhatt. The acquisition materially increased Coforge's scale, global delivery footprint & exposure to high-growth digital engineering segments.

Encora also changed the shareholding landscape. Through the transaction, Advent became the largest shareholder in Coforge, making its views impossible for the board to ignore. That's why the key takeaway may not be the resignation itself. The bigger story could be that the largest shareholder & the Chairman were not aligned on important matters. 

The bullish view is that management execution remains intact. The cautious view is that whenever Chairman, Board & largest shareholder are not on the same page, governance questions emerge and mgmt. energy is focussed away from growth.

Impact of change in EV subsidy policy from 31 July 2026

PM E-DRIVE subsidy for electric 2Ws ended on 31 Jul 2026. Govt earlier plan was to support E2W till 31 Mar 2026, then gave the industry a 4-month extension till Jul-end as there was unutilized budget

PM E-DRIVE replaced FAME-II in Oct'24 with a 10,900 Cr outlay. The idea was simple: help EV adoption scale while supporting charging infra, buses, trucks & other EV segments

initially, e-2W buyers got subsidy of 5,000/kWh, capped at 10,000/ vehicle. That was a meaningful discount for mass-market scooters. From Apr'25, cut by half to 2,500/kWh with max capped at 5,000/Veh. Signalling gradual withdrawal of support.

Now for 2W, even that 5,000 support is gone. Effective acquisition cost of an EV scooter will move up. 5,000 price hike may not sound huge, but in entry-level its imp for price-sensitive consumer

Some moderation in electric 2W demand was expected. OEMs were preparing for it as subsidy-led growth gradually transitions to product-led growth. 

August EV 2W market share came lower than July. E2W MS has come down but not in 3w as July subsidy withdrawal only 2W not in 3W. August is typically a non-festival month & seasonality also matters. OEMs should absorb subsidy via better exchange / financing offers

Market is also looking for next phase of EV support. Discussions around "FAME III" continue, but indications suggest focus could shift towards vehicle other than 2W. 2W penetration already >10% while other segment need more support

If electric 2Ws are eventually excluded from future demand subsidies, industry economics will increasingly depend on product quality, distribution, service network & battery costs instead of govt incentives.

One factor often ignored: OEMs capacity are planned in a way where capacity expansion will happen in same facility. Hence, incremental capex intensity will be far lower. Gradual drivetrain shift will continue without large incremental capex

Bottom line: Subsidy withdrawal may create short-term demand noise, but the long-term story remains the same. India's 2W market is enormous, EV penetration is still low, and the migration from ICE to EV is likely to be a long, gradual journey rather than a subsidy-driven sprint.
